newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Feb 17.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

- With 134 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media concentrated on the meeting between British foreign secretary Malcolm Rifkind and chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa and the deal of the World Trade Organisation liberalising telecommunications trade.

-- SING TAO DAILY said that putting pressure on China would damage Hong Kong's future and Hong Kong people should show they are capable of governing themselves by creating a harmonious society. It said that to maintain the stability of the civil service, Tung should appoint all the directorate officials who were willing to stay on in their posts after the handover.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL said developing countris would benefit from the deal of liberalising world communications more than the advanced countries in the long run. It said the deal would enable Hong Kong companies to enter foreign markets. The deal had also proved that the trade protectionism of some western countries had failed again, the paper said.
